claims.text: TaVCrW is initially a disordered BCC solid solution with potential to form short-range order.
Electronic excitations and magnetic fluctuations are present in TaVCrW but are not explicitly represented by the baseline EAM.
Replacing EAM+TI with MTP+FEP will reduce computational cost by more than 80%.
MTP+FEP will retain sub-meV accuracy relative to TOR-TILD.
Accurate reproduction of the ab initio phase-space distribution by the MTP enables replacement of thermodynamic integration with free-energy perturbation.
Short-range order modifies the VDOS by creating structure in its high-frequency region associated with optical bands.
Short-range order in TaVCrW produces an enthalpic stabilization of approximately 2-3 meV/atom.
Thermodynamic integration typically averages out SRO-induced VDOS and stabilization features, whereas FEP requires them to be sampled explicitly.
FEP avoids the slow sampling along a coupling parameter required by TI and instead performs direct perturbations between solid and liquid states.
A supercell containing more than approximately 100 atoms is sufficient to resolve SRO clusters and their high-frequency VDOS structure.
The 2000-2400 K interval is a regime in which SRO strengthening is diminishing but remains thermodynamically relevant.
If the supercell is too small, the MTP cannot learn SRO correlations and FEP will fail to recover the SRO stabilization energy.
Disrupting SRO creates a DAPB enthalpic cost that acts as a structural barrier.
At approximately 2000 K, the entropy contribution diminishes the strengthening effect associated with SRO.
Electronic excitations, specifically changes in the DOS gap at the Fermi level, shift the predicted melting point.
The usual GGA-PBE/LDA underbinding and overbinding rules fail for V and Cr at 0 K.
Magnetic fluctuations and electronic excitations must be included in the DFT training data to avoid V- and Cr-specific binding errors.
Neglecting high-temperature magnetic fluctuations could make the free-energy error exceed 0.5 meV/atom.
The benchmark should compare MTP+FEP and TOR-TILD on the same simpler refractory alloy using identical supercell sizes and temperature ranges.
The hypothesis is falsified if the method discrepancy exceeds 0.5 meV/atom or if cost reduction is below 80% at the required accuracy.

contradictions.description: Both fields apply a 0.5 meV/atom threshold to a difference in melting temperature, although meV/atom is an energy unit rather than a temperature unit. The threshold is coherent only when applied to the free-energy difference.
